Priya K: Heads up — CrestBank (enterprise) returned our questionnaire. Their top asks: tenant-specific key provenance, immutable audit chain for 7+ years, and a reproducible timeline for suspicious calls.
Derek M: Can you paste which questions they marked 'high priority'?
Priya K: Q1: 'Can you demonstrate that a tenant key was used to encrypt X at time T?' Q2: 'How do you guarantee audit logs are tamper-evident and verifiable by third-party auditors?' Q3: 'Please provide a step-by-step playback that reconstructs API calls without exposing raw PII.'
Liu W: They want cryptographic proof. We already emit daily signed manifests for Dedicated; Hosted has signed manifests too but with cloud-KMS signing key. Need to explain verifier flow.
Derek M: Suggest we show a Merkle-style chaining description: each audit blob -> compute SHA256 -> commit to daily manifest; manifest is signed with runtime key; manifests reference previous manifest hash (simple hash chain). Auditors can verify signature and chain integrity.
Priya K: Good. Also they specifically asked for HSM attestation for KEKs and evidence of wrap/unwrap ops per tenant.
Liu W: For Private/BYO-KMS: we can provide attestation certs (TPM/HSM) and the key manifest: {key-id, origin, attestation-thumbprint, creation-timestamp}. For Cloud KMS we can export Cloud Audit logs showing cryptoKey versions used and principal.
Derek M: I'll include a redacted CloudTrail/CloudWatch snippet and an example AWS CLI query: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Encrypt --start-time 2025-02-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-02-01T01:00:00Z
```
Priya K: They also want an 'incident reconstruction playbook' that doesn't reveal raw prompts. What can we provide by default?
Liu W: By default we provide: request_id, timestamp, route (model/version), token counts, response hashes, and request/response metadata. For raw prompt content we require tenant consent + Data Export review. We can provide prompt-hashes (sha256) so auditors can correlate without seeing content.
Derek M: We'll add an optional step: if tenant signs a release, we can include decrypted payloads packaged in an encrypted evidence bundle encrypted to their KMS key. Bundle contains: audit blobs, request traces, and a signed manifest. We'll show how to verify bundle signature.
Priya K: Nice. Let's give them verification commands in the packet. Example verify command using runtime public key: `curl https://storage.internal/manifest.sig -o manifest.sig && openssl dgst -sha256 -verify runtime_pub.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json`.
Liu W: Action: show sample evidence bundle layout. I propose: evidence.tar.gz.enc (encrypted with tenant KEK), evidence-manifest.json (signed), manifest.sig. Include `manifest.previous_hash` to chain.
Derek M: Also cover retention: Hosted default 1y; Dedicated/Private can support 7y via WORM/archive. For Hosted we can export daily blobs to customer bucket with lifecycle rules to move to Glacier/Archive. Add billing note.
Priya K: CrestBank asked whether service accounts can elevate privileges temporarily. We need to document BreakGlass vs ephemeral escalation windows.
Liu W: BreakGlass exists in Dedicated: 2-person approval + ticket & timeboxed access; Hosted: emergency access handled by ops with logged approval, but no built-in 2-person gating today. Recommend offering an SLA addendum if they require BreakGlass for Hosted.
Derek M: Also called out CVE-2026-AB12 in an adapter we use for onnx -> evidence that exploit could allow crafted model inputs to trigger unexpected file writes. They ask if it enables exfil of prompts.
Priya K: Liaise with the vuln team — what's the short answer?
Liu W: Short: vulnerability affects adapter parsing codepath. Mitigations: patch adapter (PR open), run adapter in sandboxed container, and enable read-only model artifact mounts. Exfil risk to other tenants is low given network isolation, but we should offer to run a focused test and share findings.
Derek M: I'll add a mitigation timeline and link to the patch PR.
sec-oncall-bot: Oncall: Liu W -> acknowledged.
Priya K: Proposed deliverables before our call with CrestBank: 1) Derek: RBAC + BreakGlass differences + billing blurb for long retention (due today). 2) Liu: evidence-bundle spec + sample CLI verification commands + redacted KMS logs (due EOD). 3) Priya: compile packet and schedule 45m review with CrestBank next Tue 9am ET. 4) LegalBot: prepare consent language for raw-prompt export (due tomorrow).
LegalBot: Draft consent template queued: /legal/templates/data-export-consent-v1 (assigned to Priya).
Derek M: Uploaded RBAC matrix (link). Added example IAM policies for KeyManager role and read-only audit role.
Liu W: Uploaded redacted cloud logs + evidence-bundle example (link). Included example of encrypting bundle: `gpg --encrypt --recipient crestbank-kms@keys.example.com -o evidence.tar.gz.gpg evidence.tar.gz`.
Priya K: Call scheduled: Tue 9am ET, invite sent. I'll circulate the packet 24h prior.
Derek M: One more: auditors often ask for 'who signed the manifest key' — we should include runtime key rotation history and public key fingerprints in the packet.
Liu W: Good point. We'll attach runtime_pub_rolling.json with key fingerprints and rotation timestamps.
Priya K: Thanks all. If anything slips, ping sec-oncall.
sec-oncall-bot: Thread tagged: customer-sq, evidence-playback.
Priya K: Closing for now, will re-open if CrestBank asks for deeper forensics.
